name: Infantile Digital Fibromatosis

criteria.description: Presence of firm, painless nodules on the dorsal or lateral aspects of the fingers or toes in infants or young children
Histological identification of spindle-shaped fibroblasts with characteristic intracytoplasmic eosinophilic inclusion bodies
Radiographs showing soft tissue masses without bone involvement or destruction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of typical clinical nodules plus histopathological confirmation of characteristic inclusion bodies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and histopathological; imaging is supportive to exclude bone involvement.

imaging: Soft tissue masses on radiographs without bone destruction
other: Histopathology revealing spindle fibroblasts with eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions

distinguishingFeatures: Myofibromatosis lesions often painful and can involve deeper tissues
Typically affects palmar fascia rather than digits
Usually solitary lesion in older children or adults
Histology shows histiocytic cells without inclusion bodies

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mass with pain or tenderness
Bone involvement or erosion on imaging
Ulceration or infection of overlying skin
references: Reye RD. Inclusion body fibromatosis of infancy. Arch Pathol. 1965;79:505-509.
Fetsch JF, Miettinen M. Infantile digital fibromatosis: a clinicopathologic study of 74 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 1993;17(3):231-239.
